title: What does one chlorine atom weigh?
hook: The periodic table says chlorine weighs 35.45 u. Weigh the atoms one at a time.

knows: that the periodic table lists a mass for each element
that atoms contain protons and neutrons
doesNotKnow: that atoms of one element can carry different numbers of neutrons (isotopes)
that the table's mass is an average over the isotopes found in nature

misconception: Every atom of an element has exactly the mass printed in the periodic table.
objective: The learner can explain that chlorine atoms weigh about 35 u or about 37 u, never 35.45 u, and that 35.45 u is the average over nature's mix of about 76% chlorine-35 and 24% chlorine-37.

claims.text: The periodic table gives chlorine's atomic mass as about 35.45 u.
claims.source: IUPAC CIAAW standard atomic weight of chlorine [35.446, 35.457], conventional value 35.45 (Prohaska et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 2022).

claims.text: Chlorine-35 atoms weigh about 34.97 u and chlorine-37 atoms about 36.97 u; natural chlorine is about 76% chlorine-35 and 24% chlorine-37.
claims.source: NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions: Cl-35 34.96885 u, 75.76%; Cl-37 36.96590 u, 24.24%. Weighted mean 0.7576 x 34.96885 + 0.2424 x 36.96590 = 35.453 u (node).

claims.text: Every chlorine atom has 17 protons; chlorine-35 has 18 neutrons and chlorine-37 has 20.
The stage's bag is a toy: 1,000 atoms (758 chlorine-35, 242 chlorine-37) shuffled with a fixed seed; its first 100 atoms hold 24 chlorine-37 and average 35.45 u.
claims.source: Demo.tsx makeBag(): Fisher-Yates shuffle with mulberry32(SEED = 5). Seed CHOSEN so the first 100 draws hold exactly 24 chlorine-37 (nature's share); average 35.448 u (node). Other seeds give 100-atom averages that wander by a few hundredths. A chosen seed is an illustration, not evidence (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-13 (pass 5): re-run: seed 5 first 100 = 24 Cl-37, mean 35.448 u; 242 Cl-37 in 1,000. Correction to the source: across random seeds a 100-atom mean has sd about 0.09 u (not 'a few hundredths'), so the reveal's 'average was 35.45' is a chosen-seed best case; the stage says only 'fixed seed', not 'chosen'. Builder to consider saying 'chosen' or 'lands near, not on'.

claims.text: The unit u (atomic mass unit) is about the mass of one proton.
claims.source: u = 1/12 of the mass of a carbon-12 atom (IUPAC Gold Book, 'atomic mass constant'); proton mass 1.00728 u (CODATA 2018).

claims.text: (Recall) Copper's table mass is about 63.55 u; natural copper is copper-63 and copper-65, mostly copper-63.
claims.source: IUPAC standard atomic weight Cu 63.546(3); NIST: Cu-63 62.9296 u, 69.15%; Cu-65 64.9278 u, 30.85%.

recall.question: Copper's table mass is about 63.55 u. Natural copper is copper-63 and copper-65. A single copper atom most likely weighs…
recall.why: Each atom is one isotope with its own mass. 63.55 u is the average over the mix found in nature, mostly copper-63.
